newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares end slightly higher, but near lows.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares end slightly higher, but near lows.

text.p: 1535 GMT - Swiss shares ended slightly higher, but near the day's lows following a bout of profit-taking late in the day, triggered by Wall Street's weak beginning, dealers said.

Early rises in a few blue chips, such as Roche, Novartis and Nestle, had set the stage for a generally friendly session, dealers said. Trading volumes were relatively high, but traders noted investors were mostly cautious.
* Blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended up 1.8 points, or 0.04 percent, at 4,127.3.
* Broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) added 2.90 points, or 0.11 percent, to 2,642.45.

Novartis registered shares led the active list, adding four francs to 1,586. The company is due to release its sales figures on Tuesday before the bourse opening. Roche certificates advanced 10 francs to 11,790 after a day's high at 11,930. Clariant gave up 17 francs, or 2.46 percent, to 675.
ABB slid 18 francs, or 1.03 percent to 1,727 after temporarily reaching 1,756. Sulzer fell seven francs to 937 and Alusuisse added 10 francs to 1,146.
* Among financials, insurers Winterthur and Swiss Re stood out with an advance of five francs to 938 and 22 francs to 1,391 francs, respectively.
In the case of Winterthur, speculative buying, a buy recommendation and research studies were seen behind the rise.
UBS bearer shares lost six francs to end at 1,174 after a volatile day.
Credit Suisse Group was up 0.25 francs to 141.50 while SBC gave up 0.75 francs to close at 249.

* On the Swiss Options and Futures Exchange (Soffex), demand was high for call options on insurer Winterthur on the back of speculative buying, recommendations and high turnover in Winterthur stocks in the cash market, dealers said.
Of a total of 147,006 options traded, 15,348 were Winterthur calls and 2,150 Winterthur puts. Interest was also high for options on ABB, UBS and Novartis.
